 Justē Jocytē, the first-ever draft pick of the Golden State Valkyries, is ready to bid goodbye to Ballhalla
 The first-ever draft pick by the Valkyries sees her WNBA future elsewhere. What’s next for Justē Jocytē?
 by Cat Ariail Nov 11, 2026, 12:00 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 The Golden State Valkyries are the 2026 WNBA champions, an already remarkable achievement made more remarkable by the fact that they shot under 35 percent from the field and barely 26 percent from 3 in the seven-game WNBA Finals.
 Improved shooting, it seems, will be a priority as they pursue a repeat.
 And a solution might be on their bench. Or, she might not.
 Justē Jocytē, the Valkyries’ first-ever draft pick who was selected No. 5 overall in the 2025 WNBA Draft and delayed her WNBA debut until the 2026 season, was supposed to be that shooter.
 In the summer of 2025, she suited up for her native Lithuania in EuroBasket Women and shot better than 45 percent from 3. Last winter, she played for the Spanish club Spar Girona, participating in 17 EuroLeague and 33 Lige Feminina de Baloncesto games, shooting around 35 percent from deep overall. This season, in 140 WNBA minutes across 18 games, Jocytē got up 27 3s and made 12 of them, good for over 44 percent.
 Her 3-point shooting at 6-foot-0 and soon-to-be 21 years old, plus some promise as a ball handler, suggests she could emerge as a piece who helps the Valkyries sustain their success.
 Jocytē doesn’t see it that way.
 Speaking to Lithuanian media, Jocytē revealed that she would prefer a WNBA future outside of Golden State, detailing her overall dissatisfaction with her rookie season, despite also enjoying being a member of a championship-winning team.
 Jocytē said :
 We just became champions, but from the perspective of my personal growth, it’s hard to imagine going back to the same coach, who doesn’t really communicate well and doesn’t seem to like me very much. My thoughts are that I don’t really want to return to that team.
 At ClutchPoints , Valkyries beat reporter Kenzo Fukuda dives deep into all the sentiments expressed by Joctyē, cross checking the translation from Lithuanian to English with multiple sources to offer an as accurate as possible accounting of what she shared.
 The topline takeaway is Joctyē’s frustrations with head coach Natalie Nakase. From her perspective, the coach offered evolving excuses for her lack of playing time, in addition to little clarity about her role. Jocytē indicated she understands she needs to improve, especially defensively, but believed she needed more playing time, in along with more direction, in order to do so.
 Per Fukuda’s translation, Jocytē expressed :
 It seems like I’m so hopeless on defense that I don’t stand a chance and can’t play. There were countless games where we were winning by 20 points, and they still wouldn’t let me play. You can tell that something isn’t quite right with what’s being said. If they want to develop my physicality, I should still be getting some playing time. I left without really understanding why I spent practically the entire season sitting on the bench.
 She also revealed that she approached general manager Ohemaa Nyanin about finding a WNBA future outside Golden State, with the GM simply responding, “Okay.”
 The terse response bothered the young player, while also affirming her desire to depart the organization. She related :
 And I’m thinking: wow, they had such high hopes—I was the club’s first-round pick, and there were so many expectations, they showed so much interest—but when I said I didn’t want to come back, the response was just “Okay.” It’s not exactly a blow below the belt, but it seems like they don’t really care.
 All that seems to add up to a Jocytē trade, although, despite her perceptions, the organization could desire to retain her and invest in her development. As Joctyē herself said , “As for a trade, that’s a different story, and we’ll see later, but right now my preliminary thoughts are that I really wouldn’t want to go back.”
 That said, it seems safe to assume that Jocytē’s second WNBA season will see her in a new uniform.
 As I already discussed on The Feed , Golden State’s short draft history—which, from the outside, looks like a lot of mismanagement and missed opportunities—suggests the organization might have a different valuation system for drafted prospects, making them more willing to move on from players that they, upon closer evaluation, determine to be poor fits.
 That track record indicates that Golden State will not be too precious about moving on from Jocytē.
 Cat Ariail Star 2d Swish Appeal
 How much does the draft really matter in today's WNBA?
 On Sunday, the WNBA Draft lottery results will either lift the hopes or deflate the dreams of the lotto-bound teams and fans.
 But, should it? Are high draft picks actually the most effective resource for building a team in today's WNBA?
 Because, the league's worst drafting team just won it all.
 The Valkyries' first-ever draft pick, No. 5 overall Justē Jocytē in 2025, just gave an interview in her home country of Lithuania, expressing her desire for a trade due to her disconnect with the organization.
 https://x.com/kenzofuku/status/2119888523537072256 
 In 2026, Golden State, controversially and still confusingly, traded Flau'jae Johnson, selected No. 9 overall, to Seattle for second-round pick Marta Suárez, who subsequently was cut. Their decision to cut 2025 second-rounder Shyanne Sellers also provoked criticism.
 In an alternate world, Golden State could have had Aneesah Morrow or Sarah Ashlee Barker or Mikayala Timpson from the 2025 draft, and Raven Johnson or Madina Okot or Frieda Bühner in 2026.
 Or, maybe they all would have been cut too and GSV would still be champs?
 I think all this is another example of how the Valkyries are an extreme outlier, with their strategies for sudden success not replicable for other organizations. As Zack Ward wrote before the 2026 season , teams that have back-to-back No. 1 pick usually become champs. (TBD for the Fever and Wings.)
 And maybe the rest of the league should continue to hope that Golden State fails to figure out the draft. Because if they do...
 What are your thoughts? Is all this coincidental? 
 Or, are teams better off investing their time in scouting and then signing undervalued players from inside and outside the WNBA rather than putting so much stock in adding the right player with a single draft pick?
 Rec 1 Comments Thin Stroke Comment Icon Bubble Reply Read 5 replies So, what other WNBA teams should be putting in a call to San Francisco about acquiring Jocytē? While her still-theoretical skill set could benefit most teams, these three standout to me.
 Indiana Fever
 Indiana has yet to fully install their new leadership, thus far only hiring former WNBA player Sheri Sam , who had worked in the Portland Trail Blazers’ scouting departing since 2022, as the assistant general manager.
 If the new front office opts to Iowa-ize the Fever, surrounding Caitlin Clark with more shooting and floor spacing, Jocytē could be an interesting option. Although with the Fever, like the Valkyries, focused on championship contention, the inexperienced Jocytē could find herself in a similar circumstance.
 Seattle Storm
 The Storm and Valkyries have already made an (in)famous together. So, let’s run it back!
 In contrast to Golden State or Indiana, Jocytē would fit with Seattle’s timeline, potentially becoming a fourth core piece alongside Dominique Malonga, Flau’jae Johnson and Awa Fam. A fully-realized Joctyē—a high-volume 3-point shooter with on-the-ball skills—would almost perfectly address Seattle’s deficits.
 Washington Mystics
 As Beckett Harrison has emphasized on multiple occasions, the Mystics have surround their star trio of Sonia Citron, Kiki Iriafen and Shakira Austin will a cast young players whose primary skill sets make them puzzling fits, primarily due to an absence of outside shooting.
 In DC, like in Seattle, Jocytē would address that weakness. Washington could also insulate her defensive limitations, especially if she could serve as a secondary initiator in lineups where Citron assumes primary ballhandler duties.
 Teams that simply could use an influx of young talents, like the Los Angles Sparks or Phoenix Mercury, could also make sense for Jocytē.
 What fits intrigue you the most? Do you think your favorite team should be interested? In the comments, conjure up your best fantasy trades!
